question: Can exposed weak-foot hip placement preserve currently bearing leg targets while retaining downward geometric motion and bounded joint targets?
rationale: R10AJ commands every hip in the same direction, including the load-bearing rear legs; torso motion outweighs front-leg descent. Separate placement of weak feet from commanded motion of loaded legs before another native controller.

inputs.population: All 600 nonterminal exposed partial samples, in original order. No held-out data.

variants.active_rule: Recenter only feet failing the unchanged 0.019293 Ns ordinary unilateral support gate.
Recenter only feet without an ordinary unilateral positive bearing impulse. Positive bearing is an anchor choice only, never a substitute for qualified support.

geometry.hip_model: Existing independent R10AJ gravity-projected bounded hip recentering with an explicit per-foot active mask.
geometry.knees: Keep measured angles; retain original bounded limit return if applicable.
geometry.inactive_legs: Keep both measured joint angles unless explicit bounded authored-limit return is required.

checks: All sample identities and original source report hash match.
Inactive leg targets preserve the measured pose, including exact reconstruction of the existing active-hip model.
All generated targets respect original angle and step bounds.
Record fixed-torso FK displacement and every non-downward active-foot proposal.
Report active-mask differences, all-inactive states and max per-joint change without ranking physical performance.

fixed_body_probe.source_selection: First exposed raising sample with at least one qualified foot and at least one unqualified foot.
fixed_body_probe.variants: Both declared masks, frozen at that sample.
fixed_body_probe.assumptions: Exact joint tracking, fixed torso pose, frozen contact mask. This is an optimistic geometry probe; no force, dynamics or contact update.
fixed_body_probe.stop_rule: All active hip targets equal the bounded gravity goals within 1e-12 radians, or 600 updates.

decision_rules: Do not select a physical controller based on fixed-torso motion alone.
A violation is a model failure retained with this identity; any model change after observation uses a distinct study identity.
Passing constraints supports implementing an explicitly bounded successor only after posture/contact-feedback design is declared.
Neither a positive bearing mask nor a predicted ground crossing proves support or recovery.
